products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory (上海人工智能实验室) is a non-profit, government-affiliated research institution based in Shanghai. The laboratory describes itself as focused on artificial intelligence research across areas including large models, embodied intelligence, trustworthy and safe AI, AI for Science, and foundational platforms. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten leading Chinese universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory's primary AI product is InternLM, a Chinese open-source large language model positioned for academic research, with cross-border data handling noted as a consideration. At the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference science forum the laboratory announced ten collaborative "AI for Science" results covering life sciences, materials science, and deep-space astronomy, and released a scientific discovery platform called Intern-Robotics (書生·端砚, or "Shusheng Duanyan"), described as connecting scientific large models, specialized agents, experimental data, and embodied automation equipment across the full research workflow from hypothesis to experimental verification. The laboratory also presented Intern-Robotics, a full-stack embodied intelligence engine aimed at addressing the data, training, and deployment pipeline for physical AI systems.

On the safety side, the laboratory articulates what it calls an "AI-45° balance" framework, arguing that AI safety and capability should develop in rough proportion over time, and it describes a causal-reasoning approach to trustworthy AGI organized around three progressive stages it terms broad alignment, interventionability, and reflectiveness. The held facts confirm the laboratory has a verified page on theworldofai.org, classified as a government lab, with no litigation or MCP server entries on record.
